thesis: Intuitive Machines is the leading pure-play on the commercial cislunar economy, anchored by NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program. It became the first commercial company to soft-land on the Moon (IM-1 Odysseus, Feb 2024), though both IM-1 and IM-2 (Athena, March 2025) tipped over on touchdown, exposing real landing-execution risk. The investment case is diversifying beyond binary lander missions: a sixth CLPS award (June 2026) plus a ~$148M share of NASA's $590M late-2028 Moon lander tranche, a position on NASA's multi-award Near Space Network (NSN) services contract worth up to $4.82B, and a nascent lunar data-relay constellation give the company a recurring communications-and-services revenue base. TTM revenue reached ~$334M (+53.8%), but the company remains unprofitable with thin fixed-price margins and has repeatedly raised equity. At $13.10 — down from a $46.75 52-week high — the risk/reward has reset for speculative investors who can tolerate another possible landing failure through IM-3 and beyond.

drivers: IM-3 achieves a fully upright, fully operational lunar landing, ending the tip-over narrative and re-rating the stock
Near Space Network services and lunar data-relay contracts ramp into a recurring, higher-margin revenue stream
Late-2028 CLPS tranche win (~$148M) plus the sixth CLPS award build a multi-mission backlog with revenue visibility
Goonhilly Earth Station and COMSAT acquisition expands ground-station and space data-services footprint
Path to positive Adjusted EBITDA as services mix rises and fixed-price lander margins improve
Analyst consensus Buy with a 12-month target near $39 implies large upside if execution holds

base_case.assumptions: IM-3 launches with mixed-to-successful results and CLPS cadence continues. Near Space Network and data-relay revenue grows steadily but remains early. TTM revenue sustains double-digit growth toward $400M+. The company narrows losses and approaches Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by 2027 without a large dilutive raise. Stock trades at a modest forward revenue multiple reflecting solid but not flawless execution.

risks: IM-3 or a subsequent lander suffers another tip-over or anomaly, undermining the commercial-lander thesis
Cash burn and acquisition spend force another dilutive equity raise at depressed prices
Fixed-price CLPS contracts produce persistent negative-to-thin gross margins
NASA budget pressure or Artemis re-scoping slows CLPS and Near Space Network funding
Competition from Firefly Aerospace and Astrobotic erodes IM's CLPS award share
Customer and program concentration leaves revenue exposed to a few large government contracts

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — revenue trajectory, margin progress, cash runway, and updated IM-3 / NSN commentary
Integration of the Goonhilly Earth Station and COMSAT acquisition into a broader lunar/deep-space data-services offering
IM-3 lunar mission — the next Nova-C landing attempt and key test of whether IM can land fully upright and operational
Near Space Network services task orders and lunar data-relay (Khon) satellite deployments building recurring communications revenue
NASA CLPS tranche mission (~$148M IM share of the $590M late-2028 award) plus the sixth CLPS lunar-utility award execution

key_risks: Landing-execution risk — IM-1 and IM-2 both tipped over on touchdown; another failure on IM-3 would damage credibility and the stock
Profitability and margins — thin-to-negative fixed-price CLPS margins and persistent net losses (-$109.9M TTM)
Dilution — repeated equity raises and acquisition spending pressure the share count and per-share value
Government dependency — heavy reliance on NASA CLPS, OMES III, and Near Space Network contracts subject to budget and Artemis-program risk
Competition — Firefly Aerospace and Astrobotic compete directly for CLPS awards and lunar-services share
Concentration and macro — a few large contracts drive revenue, and the stock is a high-beta (1.83) name vulnerable to space-sector risk-off moves
